title: Spend Governor: Per-customer elastic GPU selector with soft budget windows and preemptible hedging
creator: Aisha Mukherjee
description:
Summary: Implement a Spend Governor service that enforces per-customer soft budget windows and drives routing decisions between preemptible (spot) and on-demand GPU pools. The controller will operate at request-routing time to pick the most cost-effective GPU class and region while ensuring we do not exceed customer-configured spend windows. It should also decide when to fall back to cheaper model variants (quantized or smaller) under tight budgets or high preemption risk.

Goals: 1) Protect customers from unexpected spend spikes by honoring soft and hard budget caps with configurable grace periods; 2) Maintain latency SLOs by preferring lower-latency on-demand when budgets allow, otherwise use spot with hedging strategies; 3) Improve unit-costs by selecting appropriate GPU families (A100, H100, T4, or fractional/quantized paths) and model variants dynamically; 4) Provide observability (per-customer spend, projected burn-rate, routing decisions) and an API for customers to set budgets and tolerance levels.

Acceptance criteria: routing decisions are traceable in the request trace; simulated workload tests show spend reduction >= 18% for budgeted customers with <5% latency SLO violations compared to baseline; configurable soft caps trigger fallback to cheaper model variants and/or region-tier routing; rollouts support canary to 10% of traffic and automatic rollback on cost or latency regressions.

Design notes: The Spend Governor runs as a lightweight decision-service called from the Smart Router. It ingests per-customer budget windows (rolling 24h/7d) and live capacity signals (spot eviction probability, regional headroom). Decision inputs include: customer budget_remaining, preferred_regions, SLO_priority (latency vs cost), model_family compatibility matrix, and recent preemption history. The decision outputs are: chosen_region, gpu_class, model_variant_tag, and a reason_code for observability. Hedging strategy: when predicted spot_eviction_risk > threshold, route a percentage of requests to on-demand or to a quantized variant depending on SLO_priority.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Centralized vs decentralized budget enforcement — centralized service simplifies global view and consistency but is another availability blast radius; we mitigate with local caches and graceful degradation to conservative defaults. 2) Immediate hard caps vs soft windows — soft windows with a grace/decay policy avoid sudden customer outages but require robust projection math. 3) Model variant fallbacks introduce potential quality regressions; must be tied to per-customer quality targets and supported by regression alerts.

Operational plan: start with an internal-only canary using synthetic tenants in the staging cluster. Bench tests to validate cost savings across representative workloads (generation-heavy, embedding-heavy, short/long sequences). Expose metrics to Console: spend_projection, budget_usage_pct, decisions_per_min, and fallback_count. Implement audit logs and a debug endpoint to replay decisions for a given trace id.

API changes: add new fields to the routing profile: budget_window (object represented as stringified JSON in config), cost_tolerance (low|medium|high), allow_preemptible (true|false) and preferred_gpu_families (ordered list). For Linear ticket metadata we capture the spec in Confluence and a prototype PR.

Risks & mitigations: inaccurate spend projection can prematurely throttle customers; mitigation: conservative bias and cooldown periods, and a manual override to disable Spend Governor per-customer. Preemption storms could cause oscillation in routing — mitigation: moving-average smoothing and minimum routing durations (e.g., 5 minutes) before switching pools.

Next steps: finalize decision API, implement prototype in router v2, produce load test results, and ship canary gating rules to Console team for rollout control.

2025-02-17 - Marco: Reviewed and suggested adding a decay-based soft cap (grace credits) instead of instantaneous hard stops; updated design sketch accordingly.
2025-02-18 - Priya (PM): Requested inclusion of per-route quality budget so we can fall back to smaller model variants for non-critical routes. Marked customer_impact as high.

2025-02-20 - Eng spike: Prototype implemented a policy engine using rules + ML projection. Ran 24h synthetic run across three tenant profiles; observed ~22% cost reduction for budgeted tenants with latency tail increase of 3%.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/2041

2025-02-24 - Marco: Load tests revealed increased 95p latency when switching between GPU families frequently. Added smoothing window and minimum tenure on selected pool. Re-ran tests, tail latency improved to within SLOs.

2025-02-26 - Design feedback: UX needs a concise Console view for budget burn and a manual override button. Filed DES-412 for the Console mockups. Preparing canary plan to limit to 10% of traffic for two days and collect routing_metrics dashboard.
2025-02-27 - Security note: KMS integrations unchanged; audit logs added to release checklist. Set security_review_required=false for now per PM but flagged for periodic review.
